column1: # patterns.tsv - the single source of truth for this skill's vendor patterns.
# scripts/scan.sh reads this file at runtime; `scan.sh --print-patterns` renders
# the equivalent `rg` one-liners for a script-less run. There is no second copy
# to keep in sync: adding a vendor is a one-line change here.
# Format: three TAB-separated columns, one group per line.
#   1 LABEL    group name, printed in the HIT SUMMARY and above the detail block
#   2 PATTERN  a ripgrep regex, applied with `rg -in` (case-insensitive, so never
#              write case variants; use \b word boundaries against prose noise)
#   3 NOTE     optional guidance printed with the group; use it for the judgment
#              a bare hit cannot carry (what to attribute it to, what NOT to flag)
# Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored. A pattern must not contain
# a literal tab. Keep groups capability-shaped: one group per class of service,
# so the HIT SUMMARY stays readable and a new vendor usually joins an existing
# A group's absence is never evidence of a clean repo: unlisted vendors are
# found by SKILL.md Step 2's judgment pass and scanned with `scan.sh --extra`.
# Every new or tightened pattern gets a case in tests/fixtures/scan/.

column3: config files (google-services.json, GoogleService-Info.plist) prove wiring the JS never shows
the binding is never the finding - attribute it to the service behind it (R4)
MapLibre, Leaflet, OpenLayers, osmdroid are open - never flag them
client libs are MIT; the server is SSPL - the service's license decides (R1)
S3-only usage is acceptable (R4); every other AWS service stays in scope
Graph mail, OneDrive/SharePoint and Office add-ins are Microsoft-only; a plain Azure AD OIDC login is a standard protocol (R4) - report it only when Graph is called
googleapiclient, gspread and gdown reach Google Workspace/Drive APIs - same vendor, report them as Google APIs
PostHog and Matomo are self-hostable - resolve the endpoint before judging (R4)
Elastic APM, Moesif and Pydantic Logfire are hosted telemetry backends too; Elastic APM Server has an Apache-2.0 OSS build, so the Elasticsearch version behind it decides
check for a base_url override before judging (R4/R5)
attribute to the model API behind the wrapper (R4); the wrapper may itself be the abstraction

proprietary hosted LLM router, not self-hostable - attribute to Vercel AI Gateway (R4). It is OpenAI-compatible at ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1, so a swap is mostly config, but gateway: { order/only/models } provider options are gateway-only. AI SDK 5+ also routes plain string model ids ('openai/gpt-4o') through it by default unless AI_SDK_DEFAULT_PROVIDER is set - that case has no import to match
deliberately noisy - catches SDK-less vendor calls; Tier 2 prunes
Sentry SDKs are MIT, the server is FSL (source-available, not OSI) - a finding even when self-hosted; resolve the DSN host only to say which one the repo targets
named in the skill's keyword list but previously unscanned; Pusher appears in wallet/agent backends

column1: Data, search, feature-flag and CMS SaaS
column3: check the Elasticsearch version pin (7.10.2 and earlier Apache-2.0, 7.11-8.15 SSPL/ELv2 only, 8.16+ has an AGPL option) and whether OpenSearch is the actual dependency; Acquia (AH_SITE_* env vars) and the Cloudflare API are hosting-platform bindings; CKEditor CKBox/CKFinder/Cloud Services and the TinyMCE framework wrappers reach the vendor cloud unless the editor is self-hosted (tinymceScriptSrc) - resolve before judging (R5); Confluent hits are Schema Registry/serializers, not Apache Kafka itself
Zapier, Clearbit and FullContact are marketing-automation and enrichment SaaS; Mautic ships them as optional plugins
regionally critical for DPG deployments - M-Pesa/Daraja, Flutterwave, Paystack and Razorpay dominate outside the US/EU
eMudhra eSign is an Indian Aadhaar eSign service provider (ESP); check whether another ESP can be configured
read Laravel config/services.php and config/mail.php driver blocks as evidence; SMTP itself is an open protocol (R4) - the SaaS behind it is not
Twilio is not the only SMS vendor; Africa's Talking, MessageBird and Clickatell are the sole SMS path in several DPG codebases; Zoom meeting integrations are a hosted conferencing API

column1: AI/ML hosted services (beyond the big-5 LLM vendors)
column3: hosted inference, ASR/TTS, GPU-on-demand and MLOps SaaS; downloading open weights from HuggingFace is NOT lock-in, hosted inference and gated tokens are; machine translation and TTS (DeepL, Google Translate, Microsoft Translator, Edge TTS) are hosted ML too; multi-backend wrappers such as deep-translator are swappable only when LibreTranslate is configured (R5)

MapLibre, Leaflet, OpenLayers, osmdroid and OSM tiles are open - never flag them, and a repo with both a Mapbox and an osmdroid adapter is a GOOD sign (R2a); MaxMind GeoIP2/GeoLite2 and IP2Location databases are licence-key gated downloads or paid web services

column1: Web platform services (captcha, analytics tags, widgets)
column3: hardcoded tracking IDs in index.html count as evidence; mention any API token sitting beside the hit; YouTube/Vimeo player libraries and google_analytics config keys count; a pasted embed URL in content or tests does not
a hosted RPC endpoint is swappable if the provider is injected; AWS QLDB is a fully proprietary ledger with no open equivalent
Oracle and SQL Server are proprietary servers reached through open-ish drivers - the server's license decides (R1)
ad networks and store SDKs are platform rails (R4): report them, and say plainly that an adapter contains but does not remove the coupling
a catalog alias or typed accessor is often the ONLY place a module names the vendor - count them to size the blast radius; a plugin on the classpath but never applied is declared-but-dark, not usage
proves a vendor is wired even when no manifest declares it (a Podfile with no Firebase entry while AppDelegate.m configures it); Bootstrap per R2 - use for coverage, not severity
EAS Build/Update/Submit and Expo push are proprietary services on an MIT SDK; app.config.js is executable and overrides app.json - never judge from app.json alone

the library itself is closed or commercial - report it as a licence finding, separate from service lock-in; jspreadsheet-ce, survey-core/survey-library and non-Pro CoreUI are MIT - flag only the commercial editions
